The app is constantly unstable and unreliable.  Your downloads disappear, settings are lost, you're forced to upgrade or logged out unexpectedly, etc.  For somebody trying to listen while away from WiFi this will be a constant frustration.

In addition, the depth and challenge of the material seems dumbed down since the rebranding from The Teaching Company.

Still seems like the best choice for real educational material, but also a shame, given what it once was.

reviews.title: Great Courses, Inadequate App
reviews.text:
My wife and I have long been fans of The Great Courses, even during the dark time when it temporarily abandoned its name; this review is for the app, not the content.  It is flakey in its basic functionality, even after the supposedly major 8.0 upgrade:  
• It often forgets the last lecture I played, resuming instead at the beginning of the previous lecture.
• It usually loses my place when switching from video to audio.
• It stops while playing in video mode when I lock the screen.  This is a reasonable interface decision, though inappropriate for my usage in the gym.  But it usually fails to resume when I press the Play button, either on the lock screen or on my headphones.  I seem to have better luck if I pause the video before locking the screen.

reviews.title: Disappointing
reviews.text:
I love the content. I have bought a TON of content over the years. More than I’ve actually watched or listened to.  

The new Plus app is awfully dedicated to pushing the subscription plan. I don’t want a subscription. And I have no search function to just search my purchased content. Why?

Worse, this version of the app has a similar shortcoming to the old app. I download content to watch/listen when I have no internet access. But the app still insists I log in, even to watch downloaded content. 

I can’t log in if I have no internet access. I can’t log in before I leave, but sometimes it forgets, and I’m out of luck. 

Very disappointing on both accounts. I’ve been a customer since the days of cassette tapes. I think this app is deeply flawed, at least for a customer like me.

Finally, it has no search function for material I have already bought. I have to manually search. Thoughtless.

reviews.title: Awful Garbage
reviews.text:
The old Great Courses app was truly solid. I had used it across generations of iPads. Now, ever since it was retired and absorbed into the great course plus app, I’ve had THREE separate events in which I lost a few hundred GB’s of downloaded courses and thus had to redownload them.

I watch these courses when traveling. I don’t want to rely upon streaming the content, especially when my viewing progress is rarely maintained when streaming.

I’ve sunk thousands into this now piss poor company. I should have stuck with books instead. Welcome to the unreliability of the digital content world.

Furthermore, the current offerings are overtly simplified in comparison to the older courses. Many of the recent courses don’t even meet high school standards.

reviews.title: Digital Decay
reviews.text:
My “great courses” from the 20th Century are right where I left the DVD’s and still work as purchased. 

Meanwhile, Great Courses has become Great Courses Plus! 

The transition and reset of the password didn’t work; maybe because I didn’t bite your new “subscription” hook? 

At any rate, I’m writing off my lost digital purchase. Time is too precious to waste chasing locked binary information. 

I could jump through your hoops and next week a new genius executive will decide to rename it: “Great Courses Plus Plus Infinity!“ And we will all need new passwords again, to get at what we’ve already paid for. 

No thanks. I’ll just buy my Great Courses on DVD at the flea market. The old stuff is still great!

reviews.title: ADA request denied then ignored
reviews.text:
All I asked for was transcripts that are provided at an EXTRA cost. I was denied. I showed them the laws that were being violated by asking me to purchase each course, especially when I am already paying for the subscription. Then I was ignored until my YEAR subscription ended. 

Video with captions that “almost” match what is being said as it is being said, is assuming abilities and disabilities. Not everyone can read that fast, see that well, or hear well enough all at the same time! 

I’m a single parent with multiple medical disabilities and learning disabilities, using the program. I am trying to learn how to represent myself in court, to get custody back of my littlest. 

They have great courses that are in depth and of topics I want to learn more of.  I didn’t know my hearing and vision processing would decline enough for me to ask for a REASONABLE accommodation. 

If this has happened to you too, please let me know to add you to my case :(. I’m on most social media platforms.

reviews.title: Needs a Way to Ask Questions
reviews.text: I understand this isn’t a live classroom. Indeed, independent, self-paced learning is what I hoped to get. But there are instances when asking a question, a forum, perhaps, would be vital. For instance, at the beginning of the chemistry course, the professor asks, If you have 3000 students and can seat thirty students per room, how many rooms are in the school? He proceeds to talk about ways of thinking about problems in chemistry, but I was completely distracted, waiting for him to point out that, logically, there’s no way to know how many rooms are in the school, only that the 3000 students would occupy 100 of them. So now I don’t understand if that’s how I’m supposed to think, or not.

reviews.title: CC font in Ipad version of app too small; app doesn't recognize Apple's Accessibility Settings
reviews.text:
My complaint isn't with the content of the Great Courses Plus app for the Ipad. Rather, it is with the small size of the font used for closed captioning. Oddly, this app does not respond to Apple's accessibility settings. Using those accessibility settings to specify an "Extra Large Font" has absolutely no effect on the size of the font used in this app. Equally oddly, when viewing a Great Courses course with the Kanopy app, the user can use the Apple accessibility settings to enlarge the size of the closed captioning font as needed. Why viewers using the native Great Courses Plus app for the Ipad aren't allowed the same benefit is a mystery.

Even those lucky viewers with perfect hearing may at times find that using closed captioning is helpful. While the Great Courses professors tend to articulate their words well, even the best of professors will occasionally swallow a word and some will, unfortunately, mumble a bit too much. In those cases, closed captioning permits the user to more readily understand the professor. 

Although there is no set standard for the size of closed captioning fonts, the normal practice is to use at least an 18 point font. The font used in this app appears to be closer to eight points. This is an unfortunate error in the design of this app. Hopefully, it will be remedied at some point. As matters currently stand, the undersized font detracts from what is usually an instructive and entertaining experience.

reviews.title: Offline mode completely broken, also paid for courses locked
reviews.text:
This is an abysmally terrible app.
It fails at its primary function.
I downloaded a bunch of courses I own into the app to watch offline (in remote areas without internet, etc.) and the app will not start up if it doesn’t have an internet connection EVEN IF you recently used the app 15 minutes earlier on WiFi.

(I.e., I could at least understand if they wanted you to log in online once a month or so to re-authorize, but this isn’t that. The app just doesn’t start up at all without continuous internet.)

Why on earth would you take the enormous time to download everything before a trip if they render all your downloaded content inaccessible the second you’re outside of internet range?

This is on top of them intentionally and permanently breaking their “regular” app in order to force everyone onto their “Plus” app.

Which meant I had to re-download every single course AGAIN onto the new app. (Time-consuming process)
And then only to discover the new app is completely nonfunctional for offline use with downloaded courses.

I’ve spent thousands of dollars on DVDs from this company over the years, so it is heartbreaking to see them discontinue the sale of physical media, force everyone onto these digital apps, and then intentionally break their original digital app and then never get their “Plus” app (this app) to work with content you’ve already paid for.

And then on top of all of that, quite a few of the courses I’ve previously paid for are now “locked” and not available for download or streaming in the app even over WiFi because they want me to pay for those courses a second time.

I used to extol their “lifetime replacement guarantee” which is now not even worth the virtual paper it’s no longer printed on.
In fact, now they even take back courses you have previously paid for!

I strongly no longer recommend that you do business with this company.
Stay far far away.
